results.title: Master HIPAA Privacy Rule compliance confidently in 2026
results.content: Designed to ensure your security investments lower IT and financial risk, reduce costs, and accelerate revenue and compliance. HIPAA’s Privacy Rule sets a high bar for handling sensitive health information, but achieving true compliance is not about getting stuck in red tape; it’s about embedding trust and clarity in everything you do. The **HIPAA Privacy Rule** is a cornerstone regulation under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) designed to protect the confidentiality of individuals’ medical information. Key provisions include the right to access and control one’s medical records, restrictions on the use and disclosure of protected health information (PHI), requirements for covered entities to safeguard PHI, and provisions for notifying individuals about privacy practices. Understanding the key components of the HIPAA Privacy Rule is essential for any healthcare organization or business associate handling Protected Health Information (PHI). By prioritizing the implementation of the HIPAA Privacy Rule, organizations ensure patient trust, confidentiality, and compliance with regulatory requirements in the handling of sensitive health data.

results.title: How Healthcare Providers De-Identify Data for Research- iMerit
results.content: # How Leading Healthcare Providers De‑Identify Data for Research. These records consist of both structured and unstructured data, such as billing details, discharge summaries, clinical notes, and so on. Data de-identification can help in this regard. De-identified patient information in compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule enables significant medical research that benefits society at large. Data de-identification removes or alters personal information from datasets so individuals cannot be identified. This technique is essential in healthcare research, where protecting patient privacy while allowing valuable data to be used for scientific advancement is essential. This approach involves removing 18 types of identifiers from healthcare data, such as names and addresses. The expert must also document the methodology and results to support the conclusion that the risk of re-identification is minimal. In this mode, data is de-identified on demand based on a specific cohort or group of patients upon scientists’ request.
